title: Compute Profit per Product
description:
Each product has a selling price and a manufacturing cost. Compute the **profit** for every product.

**Table: products** — `id`, `name`, `price`, `cost`

Return `name`, `price`, `cost`, and `price - cost` aliased as `profit`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL(10,2), cost DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Widget A',25.00,15.00),(2,'Widget B',40.00,22.00),(3,'Gadget X',80.00,45.00),(4,'Gadget Y',60.00,38.00),(5,'Tool Pro',120.00,75.00),(6,'Tool Lite',55.00,30.00);
solution_sql: SELECT name, price, cost, price - cost AS profit FROM products ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: All 6 products returned with correct profit column

hints: Use arithmetic directly in the SELECT list: price - cost.
Give the computed expression a name with the AS keyword.
explanation: SELECT can contain arithmetic expressions. Writing `price - cost AS profit` creates a new column called profit whose value is calculated for every row. No GROUP BY or subquery needed — this is a simple column-level calculation.
